_comment: Curated recurring ANNUAL events that earn an evergreen page at /{metro}/annual/{slug}/ (kids build only). These pages hold search rank year-round ('<name> 2027' queries start weeks before dates are announced) while dated event pages come and go with the 410 lifecycle. `match` is a case-insensitive regex tested against live event titles to cross-link the current year's event page when it exists. Add entries during weekly prep when a verified one-off is clearly an annual tradition; keep descriptions evergreen (no years, no dates beyond the typical month).

bay-area.title: Hayes Valley Carnival
bay-area.description: A free neighborhood carnival that has run for over a century in Hayes Valley: games and prizes along Hayes Street, food, and a one-ring circus performance on the PROXY stage. One of San Francisco's oldest continuous community traditions.

bay-area.title: Bastille Day SF Festival
bay-area.description: The Bay Area's largest celebration of France's national day: French food, music, petanque games, a waiters' race, and family activities on Embarcadero Plaza, held the weekend closest to July 14.

bay-area.title: Japan Day
bay-area.description: Japantown's summer cultural festival from GenRyu Arts: taiko drumming, awa odori street dance, karate demonstrations, and hands-on origami and calligraphy workshops around the outdoor stage at Post and Laguna.

bay-area.title: Teddy Bear Picnic Day at Fairyland
bay-area.description: Children's Fairyland invites every kid to bring their favorite stuffed animal for a day of rides, storytimes, live shows, and the fluffiest picnic in Oakland — a mid-summer Fairyland tradition.

bay-area.title: Alameda County Fair
bay-area.description: One of the Bay Area's biggest county fairs: carnival rides, livestock barns, horse racing, concerts, and fair food across several weeks at the Pleasanton fairgrounds.

bay-area.title: Nihonmachi Street Fair
bay-area.description: San Francisco Japantown's free community street fair, held the first weekend of August continuously since 1974. Two days of taiko drumming, cultural performances, food booths, and a kids' area celebrate Japanese American heritage across the Japantown blocks.

bay-area.title: Fremont Festival of the Arts
bay-area.description: One of the largest free street festivals in the western United States, run by the Fremont Chamber of Commerce on the first weekend of August: hundreds of artisan booths, a kids' zone with rides and activities, live music stages, and festival food across downtown Fremont.

bay-area.title: Jerry Day
bay-area.description: San Francisco's free annual tribute to Excelsior-born Jerry Garcia at the Jerry Garcia Amphitheater in McLaren Park, held around his August 1 birthday since 2003. An afternoon of live Grateful Dead-inspired music that draws families across the natural grass bowl.

bay-area.title: Watsonville Strawberry Festival
bay-area.description: Watsonville's cherished downtown celebration of the Pajaro Valley strawberry harvest: free admission, carnival rides, a kids' fun zone, live entertainment, and every strawberry treat imaginable, on the first weekend of August.

bay-area.title: Bay Area Aloha Festival
bay-area.description: The Pacific Islanders' Cultural Association's annual celebration of Hawaiian, Tahitian, and Pacific Islander cultures at the San Mateo County Event Center: hula and Tahitian dance on the main stage, live music, arts and craft vendors, 'Ono food, and the Ohana Keiki Korner children's activity area. Free with a suggested donation; children 12 and under free. Held the second weekend of August since the 1990s.

bay-area.title: Gravenstein Apple Fair
bay-area.description: Sonoma County's beloved harvest fair under the oaks of Ragle Ranch Park in Sebastopol, held every August since 1973 to celebrate the Gravenstein apple: local farms, live music, a children's corral, and apple everything from fritters to fresh press.

bay-area.title: Sonoma County Fair
bay-area.description: The classic August county fair at the Santa Rosa fairgrounds: carnival rides, farm animals and 4-H exhibits, horse racing, nightly entertainment, and the famous flower show. A multi-week Sonoma County tradition for generations of families.

bay-area.title: Gizdich Ranch Apple Picking
bay-area.description: A fourth-generation family ranch in the core of Watsonville's apple country, originally purchased by Croatian immigrant Vincent John Gizdich in 1937. Apple U-Pick, which the ranch calls Pik-Yor-Self, opens in September. The Eata Nita Pie Shop, open since 1980, bakes 16 varieties of pie plus dumplings and puff pastries, and the ranch presses its own award-winning apple juice.

bay-area.title: Arata Pumpkin Farm
bay-area.description: Pumpkins have been a way of life at the Arata family farm on Verde Road in Half Moon Bay since 1932. The fall season brings the two-acre Minotaur's Labyrinth hay maze, a six-acre corn field with the Pumpkin River, hay rides, a train ride, guided pony rides, and a petting zoo. A haunted barn with live actors runs on weekend nights, and the farm keeps picnic areas open through the season.

bay-area.title: Half Moon Bay Art & Pumpkin Festival
bay-area.description: A free two-day street festival on Main Street between Miramontes and Spruce, started in 1971 by the Main Street Beautification Committee and now the coastside's signature harvest weekend. The schedule includes the Safeway World Championship Pumpkin Weigh-Off, the Great Pumpkin Parade at noon on Saturday, four music stages, a costume contest, pie-eating contests, and pumpkin carving demonstrations by Farmer Mike. More than 250 artisans sell handcrafted work alongside food vendors.

bay-area.title: Laurel StreetFair World Music Festival
bay-area.description: Oakland's Laurel District shuts down MacArthur Boulevard for a free day of world music on two stages, a Kid's Carnival, roller skating, and an artisan marketplace. A neighborhood fundraiser that has drawn tens of thousands of East Bay families for a quarter century.

bay-area.title: Christmas in the Park
bay-area.description: Downtown San Jose's free holiday tradition, produced with the City of San Jose since 1980: hundreds of decorated trees, animated musical exhibits, the Lima Train, and free Santa photos on Plaza de Cesar Chavez from late November through December.

bay-area.title: Glowfari at Oakland Zoo
bay-area.description: Oakland Zoo's holiday-season lantern festival, a family-friendly evening walk among hundreds of larger-than-life glowing animal lanterns and light displays, returning each November through December.

bay-area.title: Stern Grove Festival
bay-area.description: San Francisco's admission-free summer concert series in the eucalyptus grove at Sigmund Stern Grove: big-name acts on Sunday afternoons, picnic blankets on the lawn, and no ticket required — a Sunday tradition since 1938.

bay-area.title: Milpitas Red, White & Boom
bay-area.description: Milpitas' city-run Fourth of July celebration at the Milpitas Sports Center: an evening of live music and food vendors capped by the city's fireworks show.

bay-area.title: Hillsborough Memorial Day Parade
bay-area.description: Hillsborough's hometown Memorial Day parade and remembrance ceremony — a family-scale Peninsula tradition with local schools, scouts, and veterans' groups marching.

bay-area.title: Healdsburg Independence Day Fireworks
bay-area.description: Healdsburg's hometown Fourth of July fireworks, launched from the Healdsburg High School area — Sonoma County families picnic nearby and watch the display over town.

bay-area.title: Santa Clara County Fair
bay-area.description: The 82-year-old South Bay tradition at the Santa Clara County Fairgrounds: carnival rides, livestock and 4-H exhibits, food, and live entertainment. Since 2026 it runs the third full week of August.

bay-area.title: Sausalito Art Festival
bay-area.description: One of the West Coast's premier outdoor art shows, held Labor Day weekend on the Sausalito waterfront: hundreds of fine artists, live music, kids' art activities, and bay views.

bay-area.title: Monterey County Fair
bay-area.description: The classic Central Coast fair at the Monterey County Fairgrounds: carnival rides, livestock exhibits, food, and entertainment, traditionally the first week of September.

bay-area.title: Marin County Fair
bay-area.description: The Marin County Fair at the Marin Civic Center fairgrounds, held over the July Fourth holiday: carnival rides, live music, exhibits, food, and a famous Friday night fireworks show.

bay-area.title: Millbrae Art & Wine Festival
bay-area.description: A free, family-friendly art and wine festival on Broadway Avenue in downtown Millbrae: hundreds of artists, food trucks, festival food and drink gardens, and kids' activities. Runs the first weekend after Labor Day.

bay-area.title: Belmont Greek Festival
bay-area.venue: Greek Orthodox Church of the Holy Cross, 900 Alameda de las Pulgas
bay-area.description: An annual Greek festival at the Greek Orthodox Church of the Holy Cross in Belmont: Greek food and pastries, live music, traditional dancing, and a kids' area. Held the first weekend after Labor Day.

bay-area.title: Scottish Highland Gathering & Games
bay-area.description: One of the oldest Scottish Highland Gatherings in the West, at the Alameda County Fairgrounds: heavyweight athletics, pipe bands, Highland dancing, and kids' activities. Held Labor Day weekend.

bay-area.title: Alameda Point Antiques Faire
bay-area.description: A monthly antiques and collectibles faire on the old Alameda naval air station: hundreds of dealers of vintage furniture, records, and treasures. Timed-entry tickets; runs the first Sunday of the month through the season.

bay-area.title: Free Shakespeare in the Park: San Francisco
bay-area.description: Free Shakespeare in the Park at John McLaren Park: an annual outdoor season of 2pm performances, picnicking welcome, closing the first weekend after Labor Day.

bay-area.title: Lemos Farm Pumpkin Patch
bay-area.description: The pumpkin patch at Lemos Farm in Half Moon Bay: corn maze, pony rides, petting zoo, and pumpkin picking. Opens the first weekend after Labor Day and runs through November; timed-entry tickets sold online.

bay-area.title: Dell'Osso Family Farm Pumpkin Maze
bay-area.description: The annual pumpkin maze at Dell'Osso Family Farm, open daily in October: a giant corn maze, pumpkin patch, farm animals, and family rides. Weekdays from noon, weekends from 10am, last entry 7pm.

chicago.title: Fiesta del Sol
chicago.description: The largest free Latino festival in the country, filling a mile of Cermak Road in Pilsen with live entertainment, food, carnival rides, and a dedicated children's area every summer for over 50 years.

chicago.title: Chinatown Summer Fair
chicago.description: Chinatown's signature street fair: a lion dance procession, kung fu demonstrations, restaurant samplings, cultural performances, and a children's area along Wentworth Avenue.

chicago.title: Chicago Gospel Music Festival
chicago.description: A free weekend of national gospel headliners and local choirs at the Jay Pritzker Pavilion in Millennium Park — family-friendly and one of the city's longest-running free music festivals.

chicago.title: Chicago Urban League Back To School Festival
chicago.description: The Chicago Urban League's annual Back To School Festival at the James Compton Center in Bronzeville: free food, games, school supplies, and community resources to help families get ready for the school year.

chicago.title: All Seasons Orchard Apple Picking
chicago.description: An orchard in Woodstock where families pick their own among 16,000 apple trees, with Honeycrisp picking as the headliner. The season opens in late August and runs to the start of November, alongside more than 30 barnyard attractions including a petting zoo, pony rides, corn maze, ropes course, mini zip line, sunflower trail, apple cannon, and apple train. Pumpkin picking, apple cider donuts, fresh cider, and caramel apples make it a repeat fall trip.

chicago.title: Kuipers Family Farm Apple Picking
chicago.description: A u-pick apple orchard in Maple Park growing over 45 apple varieties, where each paid admission includes a quarter-peck bag to fill. The picking season runs from late August through the start of November, overlapping the farm's Sunflower Festival and Pumpkin FunFarm. Farmview Railway train rides, the Farmhouse Kitchen, and the Orchard Shop & Bakery keep the rest of the family busy.

chicago.title: Goebbert's Farm Fall Festival
chicago.description: Goebbert's Farm on Reinking Road in Pingree Grove opens its Fall Fest in late August and runs it through Halloween with more than 50 attractions on the grounds. Scenic wagon rides carry visitors out to the pumpkin patch to pick their own, and the farm adds a carousel, train rides, slides, animal encounters, and its pumpkin-eating dinosaur show.

chicago.title: Bengtson's Pumpkin Farm Fall Fest
chicago.description: Bengtson's has run a fall festival and pumpkin patch on West 151st Street in Homer Glen since 1981. One admission covers unlimited rides, including the Barnstormer wave swinger, egg drop, flying frogs, rooster rodeo, and rockin' rabbits, plus hayrides, train rides, a petting zoo, a corn box, gemstone mining, pig racing, and live music from the See Through Band. The farm also has a large pumpkin patch and a haunted barn.

chicago.title: Bud Billiken Parade
chicago.description: The nation's largest African American parade, held on Chicago's South Side every August since 1929 and second in size only to the Rose Parade. Marching bands, drill teams, and floats roll down King Drive to sound the call for back-to-school, then the whole crowd moves into Washington Park for a festival of music, food, and family resources.

chicago.title: ZooLights at Lincoln Park Zoo
chicago.description: Chicagoland's favorite holiday tradition: more than three million lights, a Ferris wheel, a light tunnel, Santa visits, and caroling at Lincoln Park Zoo from late November through early January.

chicago.title: Christkindlmarket Chicago
chicago.description: Chicago's German-style holiday market at Daley Plaza since 1996: dozens of red-and-white vendor booths with ornaments, gifts, pretzels, and warm treats, open daily from mid-November through late December.

seattle.title: Bite of Seattle
seattle.description: Seattle's summer food festival at Seattle Center: hundreds of food vendors, dozens of musical acts, and free admission, running since 1982.

seattle.title: Seafair Torchlight Parade
seattle.description: Seafair's signature evening parade: illuminated floats, marching bands, drill teams, and dragon dancers along the waterfront — a Seattle summer tradition since 1950.

seattle.title: Whidbey Island Fair
seattle.description: A century-old island county fair in Langley: 4-H animal shows, carnival rides, live music, and a small-town Saturday parade.

seattle.title: Seattle Outdoor Theater Festival
seattle.description: A free weekend of outdoor performance in Volunteer Park — a dozen-plus theater companies playing Shakespeare, family shows, and youth workshops across the lawns.

seattle.title: Swans Trail Farms Apple Picking
seattle.description: The u-pick apple orchard at this Snohomish farm holds over 4,000 apple trees and four varieties, including Jonagold and Cosmic Crisp, across five acres. Picking opens in September and the orchard closes for the season on October 31, with a Honeycrisp Apple Festival at the peak. A country store, cidery, and the farm's Fall Festival share the same grounds.

seattle.title: Craven Farm Pumpkin Patch
seattle.description: Craven Farm bills itself as the original pumpkin patch of Snohomish and has run a fall harvest season on Shorts School Road since 1983. Entry to the farm, the pumpkin patch, the farm shop, and the photo areas is free; a wristband adds more than ten activities including the corn maze, mini golf, and the animals, while apple cannons and paintball are sold separately. Food stands operate around the property, and barns and party rooms can be rented for birthdays.

seattle.title: Bob's Corn & Pumpkin Farm
seattle.description: Bob's Corn & Pumpkin Farm on Elliott Road in Snohomish opens its fall season in mid-September and runs it into the first days of November. Admission covers a 12-acre corn maze, hayrides out to the u-pick pumpkin patch, ziplines, big slides, a rope maze, a trike track, a gaga ball pit, a gem mining sluice, dairy barn games, and an apple cannon aimed at farm targets. A night maze runs on selected evenings starting in early October.

seattle.title: Seafair Weekend
seattle.description: Seattle's biggest summer weekend, when hydroplanes tear across Lake Washington and the U.S. Navy Blue Angels thunder over Genesee Park. The air show anchors a shoreline festival of military demonstrations, aerobatic performers, and vintage aircraft.

seattle.title: WildLanterns at Woodland Park Zoo
seattle.description: Woodland Park Zoo's winter lantern festival lines its trails with glowing animal lantern displays, light installations, and an interactive zone for kids.

seattle.title: Garden d'Lights
seattle.description: Bellevue Botanical Garden glows with more than half a million lights shaped into plants, flowers, and animals in this longtime family holiday tradition.

seattle.title: Bellevue Family 4th
seattle.description: Bellevue's free Fourth of July festival at Downtown Park: an afternoon of family activities, food, and live music leading into the Eastside's biggest fireworks show.

new-york-city.title: Thunderbird American Indian Powwow
new-york-city.description: New York's largest and longest-running powwow: intertribal dance competitions with dancers from dozens of Indian Nations, plus Native art, craft, and food vendors on the Queens Farm meadow.

new-york-city.title: Outhouse Orchards Apple Picking
new-york-city.description: The closest true pick-your-own apple orchard to New York City, in North Salem in northern Westchester County, where visitors hand-pick apples, pears, and peaches from the tree from September into October. Different apple varieties ripen on their own schedule across the season, so what is ready changes week to week. Picking is sold by prepaid bag, either a small 15-pound bag or a large 25-pound bag.

new-york-city.title: Pumpkin Picking at Decker Farm
new-york-city.description: Decker Farm, one of the four sites that make up Historic Richmond Town on Staten Island, opens for pumpkin picking on October weekends. Built in 1810 and worked ever since, the 11-acre farm is New York City's oldest continually working family farm and was designated a city landmark in 1967. Visitors search the patch for a pumpkin, take a hayride, try the bungee-powered pumpkin chucking device, and buy fall food from the snack wagon.

new-york-city.title: The Amazing Maize Maze at Queens County Farm
new-york-city.description: The Amazing Maize Maze is a three-acre corn labyrinth cut into the fields of the Queens County Farm Museum, a site that has been farmed for over three centuries and is the longest continually farmed land in New York State. Weekend visitors start with a Stalk Talk, then hunt for clues and solve puzzles on the way to Victory Bridge, where the whole labyrinth comes into view. Maze by Moonlight runs on selected October nights, when visitors bring flashlights, and parking on the 47-acre farm is free.

new-york-city.title: Hong Kong Dragon Boat Festival in New York
new-york-city.venue: Meadow Lake, Flushing Meadows Corona Park
new-york-city.description: Free racing on Meadow Lake in Flushing Meadows Corona Park, where crews of twenty paddle hand-painted teak dragon boats to a drumbeat. One of the largest dragon boat festivals in the United States, paired with a main stage of music and dance, martial arts demonstrations, folk crafts, and an international food court.

new-york-city.title: National Dominican Day Parade
new-york-city.description: Sixth Avenue fills with merengue, bachata, and more than forty floats as over ten thousand marchers celebrate Dominican heritage in one of New York's largest cultural parades. Free to watch, and easy to catch anywhere along the Midtown route.

new-york-city.title: Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree Lighting
new-york-city.description: The iconic Rockefeller Center Norway spruce with 50,000 lights and its Swarovski star, lit at a nationally broadcast ceremony in early December and glowing over the plaza daily through mid-January.

new-york-city.title: Holiday Lights at the Bronx Zoo
new-york-city.description: Millions of lights and about 400 illuminated animal lanterns across six lantern trails at the Bronx Zoo, with a holiday train, snow-tube Freeze Zone, and nightly entertainment from November through early January.

new-york-city.title: Brooklyn Memorial Day Parade
new-york-city.description: Bay Ridge's Brooklyn Memorial Day Parade — one of the oldest continuously running Memorial Day parades in the country, marching down Third Avenue with veterans' groups, bands, and local organizations.

los-angeles.title: Alondra Park Ho'olaule'a
los-angeles.description: California's largest free Hawaiian festival: live hula, island music, traditional food, and cultural booths filling Alondra Park each summer.

los-angeles.title: Nisei Week Japanese Festival
los-angeles.description: Little Tokyo's nine-day celebration of Japanese American culture each mid-August, running since 1934. The Grand Parade and the closing Plaza Festival are the two big free family anchors, alongside taiko, dance, exhibits, and food throughout the district.

los-angeles.title: Los Rios Rancho Apple Picking
los-angeles.description: Apple picking at this Oak Glen ranch runs from Labor Day weekend through Thanksgiving weekend, with early picking sometimes starting in August. Many of the apple trees are more than 80 years old; apples are sold by the pound and baskets and picking implements are provided. The rest of the property fills a full day with a petting zoo and miniature farm, tractor rides, a corn maze, pumpkin picking, nature trails, horse-drawn wagon tours, and live music on weekends.

los-angeles.title: Riley's Farm Apple Picking
los-angeles.description: A working apple orchard and living history farm in Oak Glen with pick-your-own fruit, where apples come in from September through the end of harvest. Riley's grows over 30 varieties and specializes in heirloom apples, ones bred for flavor rather than shelf life. Costumed living history adventures covering the Revolutionary War, Civil War, Gold Rush, and colonial farm life run alongside the picking.

los-angeles.title: Underwood Family Farms Fall Harvest Festival
los-angeles.description: Underwood Family Farms turns its 50-acre Moorpark site over to the Fall Harvest Festival from late September through Halloween, with a pumpkin patch, pick-your-own fruit, vegetables and flowers, and tractor-drawn wagon rides. Kids get a corn maze, hay climbing pyramids, cotton harvester and combine slides, a fun hill with tunnels and a wooden firetruck, an Animal Center, and Farmer Craig's Chicken Show. Five themed weekends — Friends of the Farm, Farm Country, Antique Tractor, Wild West, and All About Pumpkins — add live bands and roaming entertainers.

los-angeles.title: Tanaka Farms Pumpkin Patch
los-angeles.description: Tanaka Farms, a multi-generational family farm on University Drive in Irvine, opens its pumpkin patch each fall so visitors can pick pumpkins straight from the vine. The farm pairs the patch with hayrides, photo stops, and its Barnyard animal exhibit, and sells Irvine-grown pumpkins in a range of sizes and colors for carving, decorating, and cooking. The Tanaka Grill serves burgers, fries, shave ice, and lemonade on site.

los-angeles.title: Watts Towers Day of the Drum Festival
los-angeles.description: A free day of percussion at the foot of the Watts Towers, with Latin, African, Japanese, jazz, and Native American drumming traditions sharing one outdoor stage. Free tours of Simon Rodia's landmark towers run all day. Paired each year with the Simon Rodia Watts Towers Jazz Festival the following day.

los-angeles.title: Abbot Kinney Festival
los-angeles.description: Venice's signature street festival takes over Abbot Kinney Boulevard with music stages, a long run of artisan and food vendors, and a kids' zone. Run by a nonprofit that grants the day's proceeds back to Venice youth and arts organizations.

los-angeles.title: L.A. Zoo Lights: Animals Aglow
los-angeles.description: L.A.'s wildest holiday tradition: a mile of glowing animal lanterns, light tunnels, a walk-in kaleidoscope, and Santa photos at the Los Angeles Zoo in Griffith Park from mid-November through December.

los-angeles.title: Enchanted Forest of Light
los-angeles.description: Descanso Gardens' annual one-mile illuminated evening walk through glowing tulips, luminous stained-glass houses, and sculptural light art, running from mid-November through early January.

los-angeles.title: Canoga Park Memorial Day Parade
los-angeles.description: The West San Fernando Valley's long-running Memorial Day parade along Sherman Way in Canoga Park, with marching bands, veterans' groups, and community floats.

los-angeles.title: JANM Natsumatsuri Family Festival
los-angeles.description: The Japanese American National Museum's free annual summer family festival at Terasaki Budokan in Little Tokyo: taiko, bon odori dancing, crafts, and kids' activities, mid-August.

los-angeles.title: Getty Center Garden Concerts for Kids
los-angeles.description: The Getty Center's free Saturday-Sunday children's concert series on the Central Garden lawn each August: family music on a picnic blanket with free advance reservations.

los-angeles.title: Underwood Family Farms Fall Harvest Festival
los-angeles.venue: Underwood Family Farms, 3370 Sunset Valley Road
los-angeles.description: Underwood Family Farms' annual Fall Harvest Festival in Moorpark: corn maze, pumpkin patch, farm animals, and kids' activities. Open daily late September through October; weekends require advance tickets.

los-angeles.title: Los Rios Rancho Apple U-Pick
los-angeles.venue: Los Rios Rancho, 39611 Oak Glen Road
los-angeles.description: Apple U-Pick at Los Rios Rancho in Oak Glen. The season opens Labor Day weekend, with Macintosh apples first; hours vary by crop, so check the farm's newsletter before heading out.

los-angeles.title: Malibu Chili Cook-Off
los-angeles.description: An annual Malibu tradition: chili tasting, live music, carnival rides, and family fun at Malibu Civic Center. Free entry with an online ticket; runs Labor Day weekend.

los-angeles.title: Fiesta Hermosa
los-angeles.venue: Downtown Hermosa Beach (Pier Avenue / Hermosa Avenue)
los-angeles.description: The beach-adjacent arts and music festival in downtown Hermosa Beach: hundreds of artists, food vendors, live music, and a kids' carnival. Free entry; runs Labor Day weekend.

los-angeles.title: Orange International Street Fair
los-angeles.description: An all-day international street fair in Old Towne Orange: food and craft booths from dozens of cultures, live music, and family activities. Runs the first weekend after Labor Day.

boston.title: Puerto Rican Festival of Massachusetts
boston.description: A multi-day celebration of Puerto Rican culture in Franklin Park: live performances, traditional food, carnival rides, and family activities, drawing tens of thousands each summer.

boston.title: Revere Beach International Sand Sculpting Festival
boston.description: The East Coast's largest sand sculpting festival: world-class sculptors compete on America's first public beach, with a kids' zone, food vendors, and evening fireworks.

boston.title: Minuteman Library Crawl
boston.description: A week-long summer scavenger hunt across the Minuteman Library Network: pick up a free passport at any participating library, then visit libraries across Greater Boston on their featured crawl days, find each library's hidden clue, and collect stamps. Completed passports enter a grand-prize drawing. Around two dozen libraries take part, from Arlington and Watertown to Natick, Needham and Newton — a free, all-ages tradition that turns library-hopping into a family road trip.

boston.title: Honey Pot Hill Orchards Apple Picking
boston.description: A Stow orchard that is typically open for apple picking from early August into early November, with pick-your-own apples straight off the tree. Hayrides run for a small per-person charge for anyone over age three, donuts are made fresh daily, and the farm store carries produce and baked goods. The farm also books field trips, group outings, and birthday parties, making it a standing early-fall outing for Boston-area families.

boston.title: Shelburne Farm Apple Picking
boston.description: A pick-your-own apple farm in Stow, about 20 miles west of Boston, that reopens for the picking season in August. Beyond the orchard rows there are hay rides, farm animals to visit, John Deere tractor and Gator playgrounds, and a Great Pumpkin bounce house. Warm cider donuts and live music round out a classic New England fall farm visit.

boston.title: Connors Farm Pumpkin Picking
boston.description: Connors Farm has been farming on Valley Road in Danvers since 1904. Its fall season runs from early September to the start of November with apple and pumpkin picking, a giant corn maze, hayrides, and cider donuts and baked goods from the farm stand. Admission covers the corn maze, hay rides, a ropes course, jumping pillows, pedal carts, Fort Connors, and the play areas, with the Putnamville Railroad, a carousel, and a cow train on site.

boston.title: Boston Arts Festival
boston.description: Boston's only fine arts and live music festival devoted entirely to Boston-area talent, staged on the waterfront at Christopher Columbus Park. Juried artists show and sell their work while local musicians play across the weekend. Always free.

boston.title: ZooLights at Stone Zoo
boston.description: A holiday-evening stroll through thousands of twinkling lights and festive displays along Stone Zoo's tree-lined paths, with reindeer and other animal residents, from mid-November through early January.

boston.title: Enchanted Village at Jordan's Furniture
boston.description: Jordan's Furniture's free annual holiday attraction in Avon: the restored vintage animated village from Boston's old Jordan Marsh department store, plus Santa visits, ice skating, and a tube slide, from mid-November through early January.

atlanta.title: Atlanta Ice Cream & Wellness Festival
atlanta.description: A free summer Saturday in Piedmont Park combining ice cream vendors with family fitness: live music, yoga and Zumba sessions, wellness screenings, and children's activities.

atlanta.title: B.J. Reece Orchards Apple Picking
atlanta.description: A family orchard in Ellijay, about an hour north of Atlanta in the North Georgia mountains, where U-Pick apples run through September and October. As the farm puts it, for many visitors this is a tradition that spans generations. Alongside picking there is a petting zoo and other farm activities, plus a market and bakery known for fried apple pies and apple cider donuts.

atlanta.title: Hillcrest Orchards Apple Picking
atlanta.description: A self-described family friendly orchard in Ellijay offering U-Pick apples during the fall season, with weekday farm activities continuing after picking ends. The farm has a petting zoo, orchard tours, food, and photo spots throughout the property. It sits in the same North Georgia apple belt as Ellijay's other generational orchards.

atlanta.title: Burt's Pumpkin Farm
atlanta.description: Burt's Pumpkin Farm in Dawsonville opens for pumpkin season on September 1 and runs daily from 9am to 6pm through the fall. Hayrides operate in September and October, and the farm's newest stop is Autumn & Gordy's Harvest House, an interactive giant drive-through pumpkin that hayride guests pass through.

atlanta.title: GhanaFest Atlanta
atlanta.description: Metro Atlanta's annual celebration of Ghanaian culture at Blackburn Park in Brookhaven: highlife and gospel performances, kente and traditional fashion, jollof and other Ghanaian cooking, drumming and dance, and a marketplace of Ghanaian-owned businesses. Free, family-friendly, and one of the largest West African cultural gatherings in Georgia.

atlanta.title: Dragon Con Parade
atlanta.description: Atlanta's Labor Day weekend spectacle: thousands of costumed fans, marching bands, giant props and every fandom imaginable parade down Peachtree Street on Saturday morning. Free to watch from the sidewalk with no convention badge required, it is the one part of Dragon Con the whole city turns out for.

atlanta.title: Garden Lights, Holiday Nights
atlanta.description: The Atlanta Botanical Garden's award-winning holiday light show: millions of lights, a synchronized curtain of light, an ice goddess, and a tunnel of lights from mid-November through early January.

atlanta.title: IllumiNights at Zoo Atlanta
atlanta.description: Zoo Atlanta's annual lantern festival: a mile-long stroll past more than 200 hand-painted animal lanterns, with marshmallow roasts and carousel rides, on select evenings from late November through mid-January.

austin.title: Zilker Summer Musical
austin.match: zilker summer musical|singin' in the rain
austin.description: Austin's free outdoor summer musical tradition since 1959: a full Broadway-style production on the Zilker Hillside Theater lawn, Thursday through Sunday nights all summer. Bring a blanket and picnic.

austin.title: Brick Rodeo
austin.description: The Texas LEGO fan convention: hundreds of custom builds and displays from fan builders, with public exhibition days for families.

austin.title: Sweet Berry Farm Pumpkin Patch
austin.description: Sweet Berry Farm on FM 1980 in Marble Falls runs a fall season with pumpkins and gourds priced by the pound and sold by variety. Activities are paid one at a time: hayrides around the property, pumpkin painting, scarecrow stuffing, sand art, flower picking, the Sweet Berry Express barrel train, a bounce inflatable, and goat racers. Three mazes run through the season — the Candy Corn Kid Maze, the Barnyard Maze, and the larger Texas Maze — and the Pumpkin Grill serves food on October weekends.

austin.title: Bat Fest
austin.description: Austin shuts down the Congress Avenue Bridge for an afternoon and evening built around the nightly emergence of the world's largest urban bat colony. Live music on multiple stages, food and craft vendors, children's activities and a bat costume contest, all timed so the crowd is on the bridge when 1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats stream out at dusk.

austin.title: Zilker Trail of Lights
austin.description: Austin's famous holiday light trail through Zilker Park features millions of lights, the iconic Zilker tree, live music, and family activities.

austin.title: Peppermint Parkway
austin.description: COTA's holiday light experience in Austin features millions of lights, a train ride, Santa photos, and family holiday activities.

austin.title: Round Rock Frontier Days
austin.description: Round Rock's July 4th festival at Old Settlers Park: live music at the Lakeview Stage and Pavilion, food vendors, and family activities capped by the city fireworks show.

austin.title: Georgetown 4th of July Celebration
austin.description: Georgetown's family Independence Day celebration at San Gabriel Park — an evening of food, music, and family activities finishing with the city's fireworks display.

austin.title: Cedar Park Sparktacular
austin.description: Cedar Park's free July 4th festival at Milburn Park: kids' activities, live music, and food trucks through the evening, capped by the city fireworks show.

houston.title: Mayor's Back 2 School & Health Fair
houston.match: back 2 school (?:&|and) health fair|mayor's back 2 school
houston.description: The City of Houston's annual back-to-school fair at the George R. Brown Convention Center, held every early August since 2011: 20,000 free backpacks with school supplies plus on-site dental, vision, and health screenings for Houston-area elementary students. Registration required; families ride METRO free to the event.

houston.title: Dewberry Farm Fall Festival
houston.description: Dewberry Farm on FM 362 in Brookshire runs a fall festival from mid-September into November with more than 40 rides and attractions covered by one ticket. Families get a pumpkin patch, an eight-acre corn maze, a life-sized pumpkin house for photos, pumpkin painting, and barnyard animals, alongside rides such as the Barn Swinger and the Pumpkin Stroll. Parking is always free.

houston.title: Froberg's Farm Fall Festival
houston.description: Froberg's Farm, a fourth-generation family farm on West Highway 6 in Alvin, holds its Fall Festival from mid-September through early November. The corn maze gets a new design every year and the pumpkin patch is open for buying pumpkins and taking photos; the maze, Berry Fun Land, and duck races run on weekdays, while the tractor-pulled Bee Coaster, mining sluice, jumping pillow, sandbox, and pig races are weekend-only. The farm's country store, bakery, and smokehouse stay open year-round.

houston.title: Zoo Lights at the Houston Zoo
houston.description: The Houston Zoo's nightly holiday light festival fills the zoo with millions of lights, animal-shaped displays, and family activities throughout December.

houston.title: ICE at Discovery Green
houston.description: Downtown Houston's outdoor ice rink at Discovery Green opens each winter for holiday-season skating under the lights, with festive rink-side events.

philadelphia.title: Linvilla Orchards Apple Picking
philadelphia.description: Linvilla grows more than 25 apple varieties across 20 acres of orchards in Media, about 30 minutes south of Philadelphia. Apple picking starts in early August with the earliest varieties and runs through the fall as later varieties ripen into November. The farm pairs picking with hayrides, barnyard animals, a playground, fishing, train rides, and pony rides, so the orchard trip doubles as a full day out.

philadelphia.title: Pumpkinland at Linvilla Orchards
philadelphia.description: Pumpkinland has been a fall tradition at Linvilla Orchards for more than 50 years, growing out of a harvest display Peg Linvill built for the Philadelphia Horticultural Society's Harvest Show in 1971. The hand-made displays, still built each year by the farm's art department, retell the legends and lore of the harvest season along with local history, and include Peggy Ann, the world's largest rag doll from the 1985 Guinness Book of World Records. Grounds admission is free; hayrides, pony rides, straw bale and corn mazes, apple blasters, train rides, and face painting are ticketed separately, and jack-o-lanterns are lit nightly from late October.

philadelphia.title: Shady Brook Farm FallFest
philadelphia.description: Shady Brook Farm on Stony Hill Road in Yardley runs FallFest from mid-September through the end of October. The festival field has more than 25 attractions included with admission, among them the BEARS Playground, the Big Swing, a chalk truck, a chicken show, and the Alien Encounter, plus a pick-your-own pumpkin patch and a zinnia garden priced separately. After dark the farm adds the Eerie Illuminations light show, a moonlit maze, a haunted barn, bonfires, and live music.

philadelphia.title: Philadelphia Folk Festival
philadelphia.description: One of the longest-running folk festivals in North America, held every August on the Old Pool Farm about 45 minutes outside Philadelphia. Seven stages of traditional and contemporary folk run from late morning to midnight, wrapped around craft vendors, food trucks, educational workshops, camping and hands-on activities for all ages. Presented by the Philadelphia Folksong Society; children under 5 get in free with an adult.

philadelphia.title: LumiNature at Philadelphia Zoo
philadelphia.description: The Philadelphia Zoo's annual nature-inspired holiday light show: more than a million lights, wildlife light sculptures, a Ferris wheel, and Santa's Lodge across 42 acres from November through early January.

philadelphia.title: Holiday Garden Railway
philadelphia.description: Model trains winding past miniature Philadelphia landmarks built from pinecones, bark, and other natural materials at Morris Arboretum, a beloved family tradition since 1998 running from late November through December.

washington-dc.title: Larriland Farm Apple Picking
washington-dc.description: Larriland Farm has been owned and operated by the Moore family since 1973, growing over 20 crops and 90-plus varieties on a pick-your-own farm open from late May into mid-November. Apples ripen late August through October with many varieties available, and a field ticket is required to pick. The Red Barn farm market needs no ticket, and a Fall Festival caps the apple season.

washington-dc.title: Prince William County Fair
washington-dc.description: Virginia's largest county fair, held in Manassas every summer for 75 years: nine days of midway rides, demolition derbies and grandstand shows, livestock exhibitions, and fair food. General admission includes all grandstand and midway events.

washington-dc.title: Cox Farms Fall Festival
washington-dc.description: Cox Farms runs its Fall Festival on Braddock Road in Centreville from mid-September into early November. The festival is built around the farm's hayride and its giant slides, with the Cornundrum cornfield adventure, rope swings, straw tunnels, themed play areas, a goat village, a kiddie zone, and farm animals and their babies. Live entertainment, local apples, fresh cider, and Foamhenge round out a visit.

washington-dc.title: Butler's Orchard Pumpkin Festival
washington-dc.description: Butler's Orchard on Davis Mill Road in Germantown has run its Pumpkin Festival for more than four decades, opening in late September and closing in early November, Wednesday through Sunday plus the Columbus Day holiday. Admission includes access to the pick-your-own pumpkin fields, where pumpkins are weighed and paid for at checkout, along with hayrides, a corn maze, a straw maze, a corn pool, giant slides, jump pads, pedal tractors, a playground, and live music. Weekend days sell out, so the farm strongly encourages reservations ahead of time.

washington-dc.title: H Street Festival
washington-dc.description: One of DC's largest neighborhood street festivals shuts down H Street NE for a day of live music across multiple stages, local vendors, food, art, and family activities along the corridor.

washington-dc.title: ZooLights at the National Zoo
washington-dc.description: The Smithsonian's National Zoo holiday tradition: more than 100 hand-painted animal lanterns, roughly a million LED lights, train rides, and festive entertainment on select evenings from late November through December.

washington-dc.title: Garden of Lights at Brookside Gardens
washington-dc.description: A half-mile walk-through display of more than a million lights along Brookside Gardens' paved trail, a Montgomery County tradition since 1998 running from late November through early January.

san-diego.title: Volcan Valley Apple Farm Apple Picking
san-diego.description: Julian's u-pick apple farm spreads 7,000-plus trellis-grown trees and seven apple varieties across 10 scenic acres, picking from late August through mid-October as weather and crop permit. The trellis system keeps fruit low and reachable for pickers of every age and height, from toddlers just learning to walk to grandparents who prefer to keep their feet on the ground. Wide rows between the trees make it stroller and family friendly.

san-diego.title: Bates Nut Farm Pumpkin Patch
san-diego.description: Families have been coming to Bates Nut Farm's pumpkin patch in Valley Center since 1963. From mid-September through Halloween the century-old farm runs tractor hayrides, a straw maze, pony rides, a petting corral, a corn pit, and an inflatable bounce house, with face painting, a rock climbing wall, kids' crafts, caricatures, a mechanical bull, an inflatable slide, and live local bands added on weekends. The farm's zoo is free and open year-round.

san-diego.title: Hillcrest CityFest
san-diego.description: San Diego's largest free street festival closes seven blocks of 5th Avenue in Hillcrest for live bands, DJs, street performers, and hundreds of art and food vendors. A dedicated Kids Zone at the south end runs crafts and storytime through the afternoon.

san-diego.title: Jungle Bells at the San Diego Zoo
san-diego.description: The San Diego Zoo's holiday celebration brings nightly music, reindeer games, holiday light displays, and Santa visits through December.

san-diego.title: December Nights at Balboa Park
san-diego.description: San Diego's free two-day holiday festival at Balboa Park features a tree lighting, dozens of performances, free museum access, and a family zone.

honolulu.title: Duke Kahanamoku OceanFest
honolulu.description: Waikiki's multi-day celebration of Duke Kahanamoku, held each August around his birthday: ocean sports across surfing, paddling, and swimming, a keiki surf festival, the opening ceremony at Kuhio Beach, and the birthday lei draping at the Duke statue. Many shoreline events are free to watch.

honolulu.title: Aloun Farms Pumpkin Fall Festival
honolulu.description: Aloun Farms in Kapolei holds its Pumpkin Fall Festival across weekends in October, an island tradition the farm has now run for more than two decades. Visitors pick their own pumpkins in the field, shop the Country Market for locally grown produce and local vendors, take photos in the sunflowers, and watch family entertainment on the farm.

honolulu.title: Honolulu City Lights
honolulu.description: The City and County of Honolulu's annual holiday celebration at Honolulu Hale features a giant tree lighting, Shaka Santa, and an electric light parade.

honolulu.title: Holidays with the Animals
honolulu.description: The Honolulu Zoo's December tradition has zoo animals unwrap holiday gifts, with Santa visits and keiki crafts at the zoo.

honolulu.title: Kauai Hospice Concert in the Sky
honolulu.description: Kauai's signature July 4th benefit for Kauai Hospice at Vidinha Stadium in Lihue — an all-day family festival of live music and food ending with the island's largest fireworks show.

phoenix.title: Schnepf Farms Pumpkin & Chili Party
phoenix.description: Schnepf Farms calls the Pumpkin & Chili Party its signature fall festival, and it has run every October in Queen Creek for more than 25 years. The farm sets up a corn maze, hayrides, pumpkin patch picking, a petting zoo, amusement rides, pig races, and entertainment shows. Evenings bring bonfires with music on the farm.

phoenix.title: Vertuccio Farms Fall Festival
phoenix.description: Vertuccio Farms on South Power Road in Mesa runs a month-long Fall Festival built around its five-acre corn maze, an event the farm counts in its twenty-eighth year. One admission covers the maze, a petting zoo, mini golf, a barrel train ride, a ropes course, a pig race ride, a giant jump pad, a giant tube roll, the super mega slide, carnival games, and a playground. Pumpkins are priced by size and sold in the farm's Pumpkin Barn alongside straw bales and corn stalks.

phoenix.title: ZooLights at the Phoenix Zoo
phoenix.description: The Phoenix Zoo's holiday light festival features millions of lights, life-size animal lanterns, a light tunnel, and nightly family entertainment.

phoenix.title: Las Noches de las Luminarias
phoenix.description: Desert Botanical Garden's holiday tradition lights the desert landscape with thousands of luminarias, live music, and Santa visits.

dallas-fort-worth.title: Autumn at the Arboretum & Pumpkin Village
dallas-fort-worth.description: Autumn at the Arboretum fills the Dallas Arboretum's gardens with more than 100,000 pumpkins, gourds, and squash from mid-September to the start of November, anchored by the nationally known Pumpkin Village display houses. The village is rebuilt around a new design theme each season. The run also includes a pumpkin and squash show and sale, printmaking and mosaic workshops, garden sketchbook journaling, and seasonal cooking classes; timed admission tickets are reserved online.

dallas-fort-worth.title: Hall's Pumpkin Farm and Corn Maze
dallas-fort-worth.venue: Hall's Pumpkin Farm and Corn Maze
dallas-fort-worth.description: Hall's Pumpkin Farm on Hall-Johnson Road in Grapevine opens for a short fall season starting in early October and closing in the first days of November. The pumpkin patch has scarecrow, hay bale, farm animal, and vintage tractor photo setups, and tractor-pulled hayrides let daytime riders feed the animals. The corn maze runs to more than two acres of thickly planted corn and can also be walked after dark with a flashlight; the farm is cash only.

dallas-fort-worth.title: Plano Balloon Festival
dallas-fort-worth.description: North Texas's hot air balloon weekend at Oak Point Park, running for more than four decades. Dozens of balloons inflate and launch at dawn and again at dusk, with an evening balloon glow, a main stage, kids activities, skydivers, a fun run and fair food across four days each September.

dallas-fort-worth.title: Holiday at the Arboretum
dallas-fort-worth.description: The Dallas Arboretum's holiday celebration features the famous 12 Days of Christmas gazebo displays, a Christmas village, and Santa visits.

dallas-fort-worth.title: ICE! at Gaylord Texan
dallas-fort-worth.description: The centerpiece of Gaylord Texan's Lone Star Christmas, ICE! is a massive hand-carved ice sculpture attraction with slides, plus millions of lights and family activities.

miami.title: The Berry Farm Harvest Festival
miami.description: The Berry Farm's Harvest Festival runs from mid-September into November across 40 acres on SW 216th Street in Miami's southern farm country. The festival has a five-acre corn maze, a pumpkin patch with photo setups and pumpkins for sale, hayrides through the farm, shaded play areas, sunflower fields, and live music on weekends. On selected Fridays and Sundays in October and November the farm stays open until 9pm.

miami.title: The Children's Trust Family Expo
miami.description: Miami-Dade's largest free family resource fair, held each August as the school year approaches. Hundreds of exhibitors cover after-school programs, child care, health and wellness, special-needs services and enrichment in arts, sports and STEM, wrapped around a day of live performances, games, face painting and balloon artists. Free admission, run by The Children's Trust.

miami.title: Zoo Lights Miami
miami.description: Zoo Miami's after-hours holiday light display transforms the zoo into a glowing wonderland with a giant LED tree, holiday music, and Santa appearances.

miami.title: NightGarden at Fairchild
miami.description: Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden's holiday light experience fills the gardens with glowing installations, an interactive talking tree, and family activities.
